verdict.rationale: LangSmith's evaluation docs list "Code rules" as a first-class evaluator type for scoring experiments, alongside LLM-as-judge and pairwise comparison. Code-style checks such as format validation and quality heuristics can also run automatically on production traces, so code-based scoring is a documented native capability. The evidence is only a bullet-point mention, though, with no detail on how custom scorer functions are authored. Missing for 10: documentation of authoring custom evaluator functions via the SDK (signatures, returned scores/feedback keys), custom aggregate/summary metrics, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
